prose.text: Import Badge and the BadgeProps type from @tensquads/ui/react. Badge is a plain, non-interactive <span> because UI SDK does not ship a Badge component or behavior for this label. It has no hand-authored ARIA role and is not focusable.

tone accepts default, success, warning, danger, or info (default default). The default tone uses the primary soft surface with secondary text. Status tones use the matching semantic surface. Their text uses the status text token in light themes and the surface-text token in dark themes so the 12px labels keep readable contrast. Dark danger uses red-300 because danger-surface-text falls below the contrast target on the danger surface. Keep a state name in the visible text; color alone does not convey the state.
All other props follow the native span API. Badge does not open a menu. The OpenUI definition accepts a visible label and tone because OpenUI props are serializable.
Import Button and the ButtonProps type from @tensquads/ui/react. It wraps UI SDK's Button from @ui-sdk/react/button and keeps its native button behavior, data-slot, render prop, and forwarded props.

variant accepts solid, soft, outline, ghost, or danger (default solid). size accepts sm, md, or lg (default md). pill makes the corners fully rounded. iconOnly sizes an icon-only button and requires an aria-label. Pass icons as React children; this task does not port the Agent-UI icon set.

The danger variant uses gray-0 text in light mode and maps its component text property to gray-1000 in explicit and system dark modes. Both tokens resolve to white in their respective themes, matching the white text specified for danger-solid.

All other props follow the UI SDK Button API. It supports native button props, pending async actions, focusable disabled state, and rendering a link through render. Use a clear text label unless the button contains only an icon.
The OpenUI definition accepts a visible label, variant, size, pill, and disabled. It does not accept arbitrary icon nodes because OpenUI props are serializable.
Import Chip and ChipProps from @tensquads/ui/react. Chip wraps UI SDK Button from @ui-sdk/react/button. A chip opens an attached object, so it uses button action behavior without a pressed state.

name is the object's identifier, including snake_case names. icon is a required React node and is hidden from assistive technology because the visible name labels the button. Pass null for no icon. Supply onClick to open the object, or use render with a link to its destination. All remaining props follow the UI SDK Button API, including disabled and className.

The chip is a primary-soft pill with a minimum height of 28px. Its icon uses text-secondary; its name uses button-md. Hover uses primary-soft-hover. Long identifiers remain visible and can wrap inside the pill, increasing its height.

OpenUI requires Chip(name, icon, href). Supply the object identifier, a serializable icon glyph string, and the object's destination URL. It renders Chip through UI SDK Button's render prop as an anchor to href. Mouse click and Enter open the destination. Space follows native link behavior. React consumers can still supply a React node icon and an onClick action or render element.

Import Dialog, its parts, and the matching prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. Dialog wraps UI SDK's @ui-sdk/react/dialog parts: Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogBackdrop, DialogContent, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, and DialogClose. Each part keeps its UI SDK data-slot, render prop, open-state API, and forwarded props. The wrapper adds Agent-UI classes only.

Use all required parts and include a DialogTitle in every dialog. Use a visible trigger label. Dialog is modal by default. UI SDK manages focus, Tab containment, Escape and backdrop dismissal, scroll lock, and focus return. Use the root's open and onOpenChange props for controlled state, or defaultOpen for an initially open dialog. DialogContent supports initialFocus, finalFocus, and keepMounted.

The OpenUI definition accepts serializable triggerLabel, title, description, body, cancelLabel, actionLabel, and destructive props. Both actions dismiss the dialog. The OpenUI view loads its Dialog parts after mounting in the browser. It renders no server content or loading placeholder.

The content uses panel, panel-border, radius-2xl, shadow-overlay, and panel title and description typography tokens. The backdrop uses duration-exit and ease-exit for opacity transitions. The content uses duration-enter and ease-enter for opacity and scale transitions. Reduced-motion preferences disable transitions. Layout uses logical properties and constrains the content to the viewport.

Import Field, FieldLabel, FieldControl, FieldDescription, FieldError, and their prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. These parts wrap UI SDK's field entry and preserve its root, label, control, description, and error slots, render props, state, and forwarded props. Place Input inside the field so UI SDK connects the label, description, and validation state to it.

The root accepts UI SDK field props such as name, disabled, and invalid. A FieldLabel names the control. FieldDescription supplies help text. By default, FieldError shows validation errors after a submit attempt, or immediately with invalid. For a custom error, pass invalid to Field and match={true} to FieldError. The FieldControl part is available for another native input control.

The OpenUI definition produces a complete text field from label, name, optional placeholder, value, description, error, disabled, and readOnly. This definition does not accept event handlers or arbitrary React nodes.

FieldSet, FieldLegend, and FieldGroup, with their prop types, wrap the remaining public field parts. Keep the legend first so it names the set. A description directly inside the set describes the group. Disabling the set disables its controls. Each part preserves SDK slots, render, class callbacks, and native props.
OpenUI values update as the stream grows. The field remains editable after generation. Use React for field-set compositions; this OpenUI definition exposes only a single text field.

Import Input and InputProps from @tensquads/ui/react. Input wraps UI SDK's Input from @ui-sdk/react/input, preserving its native input, data-slot, render, value handling, and forwarded props. Use it in a Field or provide an aria-label.
variant is soft (default) or outline. The value API accepts defaultValue, or value with onValueChange(value, details). Native input props include disabled, readOnly, and placeholder.
The OpenUI definition accepts a required accessible label, placeholder, value, variant, disabled, and readOnly. This definition does not accept event handlers or arbitrary React nodes.

InputGroup and InputClear, with InputGroupProps and InputClearProps, wrap the remaining public input parts. Put Input and a named InputClear inside InputGroup. The clear button appears when text can be cleared. Pressing it clears the value, reports clear-press, and focuses the input. All parts preserve SDK slots, render, class callbacks, and native props.
OpenUI values update as the stream grows. The input remains editable after generation. Use React for group compositions; this OpenUI definition exposes only a single input.

Import Menu, its parts, and their prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. It wraps the UI SDK Menu from @ui-sdk/react/menu. The exported parts keep the SDK slots, render prop, forwarded props, and action callback shape.

Compose Menu, MenuTrigger, and MenuContent, then add MenuItem and MenuSeparator as needed. Use defaultOpen for an uncontrolled menu, or open with onOpenChange(open, details) for controlled state. The default MenuTrigger renders our Button. Supply visible children or an accessible name; the trigger adds no fallback label. Pass render to the trigger to use another element. MenuContent defaults to the SDK placement behavior; side="bottom" and align="start" keep its start edge aligned with the reading direction in RTL.

Each MenuItem accepts a serializable value and reports it through Menu's onAction(value, details). UI SDK handles Enter, Space, ArrowDown, arrow navigation, typeahead, Escape, outside press, focus return, and disabled-item focus. It also supports groups, shortcuts, icons, async actions, and submenus through the exported SDK parts. A disabled item stays focusable but cannot run.

The OpenUI definition accepts a non-empty trigger label and an items array with one to six actions. Each action requires non-empty label and value strings. The optional danger and disabled flags default to false. At most one action can be destructive. The renderer validates these limits before rendering; invalid props produce a Menu render error through TensquadsRenderer's onError callback. OpenUI streams cannot serialize action functions. The OpenUI renderer dispatches a tensquads:menu-action CustomEvent on document with { value } in detail. A client can listen for that event and run the matching local action. Hand-built React menus use the UI SDK onAction(value, details) callback instead.

OpenUI places the destructive action last, after a separator. For hand-built React menus, place a MenuItem with destructive last and add the separator yourself. Menu styles use Agent-UI surface, border, shadow, radius, motion, and danger color tokens. Popup placement and collision handling come from UI SDK and follow page direction.

Import SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem and SegmentedControlIndicator from @tensquads/ui/react. They wrap UI SDK's public segmented-control parts from @ui-sdk/react/segmented-control and preserve their slots, render props, value callbacks and forwarded props.

Set a visible external label or aria-label. Put the indicator and two to four items inside the root. Each item needs a stable value. Use defaultValue or controlled value with onValueChange(value, details). Use this for exclusive modes, not actions.

UI SDK provides radio-group semantics, one tab stop, focus management, and arrow-key selection, skipping disabled items and wrapping by default. Left and right follow the page direction: in RTL, the physical arrow navigation reverses. Space selects the focused item; Enter submits its form.

The OpenUI definition accepts a label, two to four distinct text options and an optional initial value from those options. Its schema rejects duplicate options and values outside the option set. During streaming, each option keeps its identity as its text grows. Duplicate labels keep their item nodes. Only one copy is selectable: the focused copy, then the user-selected copy, then the first copy. Other copies are disabled until their text becomes distinct. An unmatched initial value is deferred, with the first available option selected until it matches. A user selection takes precedence over the initial value. Consumers can provide icon content through React children and must give icon-only items accessible names.

Import Squadmate and the SquadmateProps type from @tensquads/ui/squadmates or @tensquads/ui/react. The component renders an accessible agent image. It accepts an agent slug, an AgentState, a square pixel size (default 64), and a locale for the accessible name (default en). The image is not interactive and is not in the tab order.

The component takes a character slug such as petra. The roster and drawing APIs in @tensquads/ui/squadmates use role IDs such as master. Use AGENT_ROLE_TO_SLUG and AGENT_SLUG_TO_ROLE from @tensquads/ui/schemas to convert between them. That entry also exports AgentRoleSchema, AgentSlugSchema, and AgentStateSchema with their inferred types.

SQUADMATES contains the roster. AGENT_LOOP_STATES contains the loop states; SquadmateDrawState also includes idle. squadmateMarkup(imageId, state, size) returns SVG markup. It throws UnknownSquadmateError for an unknown role ID and UnknownSquadmateStateError for an unknown state. Sizes below 64 px show the upper body; sizes of 64 px or more show the whole mascot. SQUADMATE_CSS contains optional blink styles for inline markup and disables the animation for reduced motion. The React image does not include those styles.
The image name contains the localized character name and state. For example, English Petra, Planning and Arabic بترا، تخطيط.
Arabic names follow the website copy in tensquads-website/src/components/home/copy.ar.ts. English names follow its copy.en.ts entries and match the roster. Arabic state labels follow PLAN.md D18.

Mascot palettes and artwork colours are drawing source data in packages/ui/src/squadmates/mascots.ts. State badge colours are in packages/ui/src/squadmates/draw.ts. These colours are embedded in SVG markup. Roster colour fields remain source metadata in packages/ui/src/squadmates/roster.ts. They are not component CSS tokens.
OpenUI is useful when an agent needs to include an identified squadmate image in a generated response. The definition exposes the same props and validates them with shared schemas.

Import Switch and SwitchThumb from @tensquads/ui/react. They wrap the UI SDK switch parts from @ui-sdk/react/switch and preserve their slots, render props, checked state, callbacks and forwarded props.

Use defaultChecked or controlled checked with onCheckedChange(checked, details). Give the switch a visible external label or aria-label. disabled, readOnly, required, name and value follow the UI SDK API. Space toggles the switch; Enter does not.
The UI SDK implements switch semantics and keyboard handling. It does not use arrow navigation for a standalone switch. Track motion mirrors in RTL. Reduced-motion preferences disable the transition.

The OpenUI definition accepts a label, initial checked state and disabled state. During streaming, arriving initial values update the checked state until the user interacts. The user's choice takes precedence over later initial values.

Import Tooltip, its parts, and their prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. It wraps the UI SDK Tooltip from @ui-sdk/react/tooltip and keeps its root, trigger, content, arrow, and shortcut parts, data-slot values, render props, placement, open and delay options, and forwarded props.

Use Tooltip with TooltipTrigger and TooltipContent. TooltipArrow and TooltipShortcut are optional. UI SDK opens the hint on hover and keyboard focus and closes it on Escape. By default, it describes a named trigger with aria-describedby and names an unnamed trigger with the tooltip text. Set type="label" or type="description" to override this choice. Keep an icon-only button's own aria-label when the tooltip provides extra help. For touch-only help buttons, set toggleable.

TooltipContent accepts side and align values documented by UI SDK. start and end sides follow the reading direction, while data-side reports the physical side after placement and collision handling. The root accepts open, defaultOpen, delay, closeDelay, disabled, toggleable, closeOnPress, type, and shortcut props as documented by UI SDK.

The OpenUI definition accepts an accessible trigger label, short hint, and side. Fixtures render a named icon-only button with a tooltip because a tooltip has no meaningful standalone output without a trigger.

The default MenuTrigger renders our Button. Supply visible children or an accessible name; the trigger adds no fallback label. Pass render to the trigger to use another element. MenuContent defaults to the SDK placement behavior; side="bottom" and align="start" keep its start edge aligned with the reading direction in RTL.

Each MenuItem accepts a serializable value and reports it through Menu's onAction(value, details). The OpenUI definition accepts a non-empty trigger label and an items array with one to six actions. Each action requires non-empty label and value strings. The optional danger and disabled flags default to false. At most one action can be destructive. The renderer validates these limits before rendering; invalid props produce a Menu render error through TensquadsRenderer's onError callback. OpenUI streams cannot serialize action functions. The OpenUI renderer dispatches a tensquads:menu-action CustomEvent on document with { value } in detail. A client can listen for that event and run the matching local action. Hand-built React menus use the UI SDK onAction(value, details) callback instead.

OpenUI places the destructive action last, after a separator. For hand-built React menus, place a MenuItem with destructive last and add the separator yourself. Menu styles use Agent-UI surface, border, shadow, radius, motion, and danger color tokens. Popup placement and collision handling come from UI SDK and follow page direction.

Set a visible external label or aria-label. Put the indicator and two to four items inside the root. Each item needs a stable value. Use defaultValue or controlled value with onValueChange(value, details). Use this for exclusive modes, not actions.

UI SDK provides radio-group semantics, one tab stop, focus management, and arrow-key selection, skipping disabled items and wrapping by default. Left and right follow the page direction: in RTL, the physical arrow navigation reverses. Space selects the focused item; Enter submits its form.

The OpenUI definition accepts a label, two to four distinct text options and an optional initial value from those options. Its schema rejects duplicate options and values outside the option set. During streaming, each option keeps its identity as its text grows. Duplicate labels keep their item nodes. Only one copy is selectable: the focused copy, then the user-selected copy, then the first copy. Other copies are disabled until their text becomes distinct. An unmatched initial value is deferred, with the first available option selected until it matches. A user selection takes precedence over the initial value. Consumers can provide icon content through React children and must give icon-only items accessible names.

Arabic names follow the website copy in tensquads-website/src/components/home/copy.ar.ts. English names follow its copy.en.ts entries and match the roster. Arabic state labels follow PLAN.md D18.

TooltipContent accepts side and align values documented by UI SDK. start and end sides follow the reading direction, while data-side reports the physical side after placement and collision handling. The root accepts open, defaultOpen, delay, closeDelay, disabled, toggleable, closeOnPress, type, and shortcut props as documented by UI SDK.

The OpenUI definition accepts an accessible trigger label, short hint, and side. Fixtures render a named icon-only button with a tooltip because a tooltip has no meaningful standalone output without a trigger.

Import Badge and the BadgeProps type from @tensquads/ui/react. Badge is a plain, non-interactive <span> because UI SDK does not ship a Badge component or behavior for this label. It has no hand-authored ARIA role and is not focusable.

tone accepts default, success, warning, danger, or info (default default). The default tone uses the primary soft surface with secondary text. Status tones use the matching semantic surface. Their text uses the status text token in light themes and the surface-text token in dark themes so the 12px labels keep readable contrast. Dark danger uses red-300 because danger-surface-text falls below the contrast target on the danger surface. Keep a state name in the visible text; color alone does not convey the state.
All other props follow the native span API. Badge does not open a menu. The OpenUI definition accepts a visible label and tone because OpenUI props are serializable.
Import Button and the ButtonProps type from @tensquads/ui/react. It wraps UI SDK's Button from @ui-sdk/react/button and keeps its native button behavior, data-slot, render prop, and forwarded props.

variant accepts solid, soft, outline, ghost, or danger (default solid). size accepts sm, md, or lg (default md). pill makes the corners fully rounded. iconOnly sizes an icon-only button and requires an aria-label. Pass icons as React children; this task does not port the Agent-UI icon set.

The danger variant uses gray-0 text in light mode and maps its component text property to gray-1000 in explicit and system dark modes. Both tokens resolve to white in their respective themes, matching the white text specified for danger-solid.

All other props follow the UI SDK Button API. It supports native button props, pending async actions, focusable disabled state, and rendering a link through render. Use a clear text label unless the button contains only an icon.
The OpenUI definition accepts a visible label, variant, size, pill, and disabled. It does not accept arbitrary icon nodes because OpenUI props are serializable.
Import Chip and ChipProps from @tensquads/ui/react. Chip wraps UI SDK Button from @ui-sdk/react/button. A chip opens an attached object, so it uses button action behavior without a pressed state.

name is the object's identifier, including snake_case names. icon is a required React node and is hidden from assistive technology because the visible name labels the button. Pass null for no icon. Supply onClick to open the object, or use render with a link to its destination. All remaining props follow the UI SDK Button API, including disabled and className.

The chip is a primary-soft pill with a minimum height of 28px. Its icon uses text-secondary; its name uses button-md. Hover uses primary-soft-hover. Long identifiers remain visible and can wrap inside the pill, increasing its height.

OpenUI requires Chip(name, icon, href). Supply the object identifier, a serializable icon glyph string, and the object's destination URL. It renders Chip through UI SDK Button's render prop as an anchor to href. Mouse click and Enter open the destination. Space follows native link behavior. React consumers can still supply a React node icon and an onClick action or render element.

Import Dialog, its parts, and the matching prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. Dialog wraps UI SDK's @ui-sdk/react/dialog parts: Dialog, DialogTrigger, DialogBackdrop, DialogContent, DialogTitle, DialogDescription, and DialogClose. Each part keeps its UI SDK data-slot, render prop, open-state API, and forwarded props. The wrapper adds Agent-UI classes only.

Use all required parts and include a DialogTitle in every dialog. Use a visible trigger label. Dialog is modal by default. UI SDK manages focus, Tab containment, Escape and backdrop dismissal, scroll lock, and focus return. Use the root's open and onOpenChange props for controlled state, or defaultOpen for an initially open dialog. DialogContent supports initialFocus, finalFocus, and keepMounted.

The OpenUI definition accepts serializable triggerLabel, title, description, body, cancelLabel, actionLabel, and destructive props. Both actions dismiss the dialog. The OpenUI view loads its Dialog parts after mounting in the browser. It renders no server content or loading placeholder.

The content uses panel, panel-border, radius-2xl, shadow-overlay, and panel title and description typography tokens. The backdrop uses duration-exit and ease-exit for opacity transitions. The content uses duration-enter and ease-enter for opacity and scale transitions. Reduced-motion preferences disable transitions. Layout uses logical properties and constrains the content to the viewport.

Import Field, FieldLabel, FieldControl, FieldDescription, FieldError, and their prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. These parts wrap UI SDK's field entry and preserve its root, label, control, description, and error slots, render props, state, and forwarded props. Place Input inside the field so UI SDK connects the label, description, and validation state to it.

The root accepts UI SDK field props such as name, disabled, and invalid. A FieldLabel names the control. FieldDescription supplies help text. By default, FieldError shows validation errors after a submit attempt, or immediately with invalid. For a custom error, pass invalid to Field and match={true} to FieldError. The FieldControl part is available for another native input control.

The OpenUI definition produces a complete text field from label, name, optional placeholder, value, description, error, disabled, and readOnly. This definition does not accept event handlers or arbitrary React nodes.

FieldSet, FieldLegend, and FieldGroup, with their prop types, wrap the remaining public field parts. Keep the legend first so it names the set. A description directly inside the set describes the group. Disabling the set disables its controls. Each part preserves SDK slots, render, class callbacks, and native props.
OpenUI values update as the stream grows. The field remains editable after generation. Use React for field-set compositions; this OpenUI definition exposes only a single text field.

Import Input and InputProps from @tensquads/ui/react. Input wraps UI SDK's Input from @ui-sdk/react/input, preserving its native input, data-slot, render, value handling, and forwarded props. Use it in a Field or provide an aria-label.
variant is soft (default) or outline. The value API accepts defaultValue, or value with onValueChange(value, details). Native input props include disabled, readOnly, and placeholder.
The OpenUI definition accepts a required accessible label, placeholder, value, variant, disabled, and readOnly. This definition does not accept event handlers or arbitrary React nodes.

InputGroup and InputClear, with InputGroupProps and InputClearProps, wrap the remaining public input parts. Put Input and a named InputClear inside InputGroup. The clear button appears when text can be cleared. Pressing it clears the value, reports clear-press, and focuses the input. All parts preserve SDK slots, render, class callbacks, and native props.
OpenUI values update as the stream grows. The input remains editable after generation. Use React for group compositions; this OpenUI definition exposes only a single input.

Import Menu, its parts, and their prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. It wraps the UI SDK Menu from @ui-sdk/react/menu. The exported parts keep the SDK slots, render prop, forwarded props, and action callback shape.

Compose Menu, MenuTrigger, and MenuContent, then add MenuItem and MenuSeparator as needed. Use defaultOpen for an uncontrolled menu, or open with onOpenChange(open, details) for controlled state. The default MenuTrigger renders our Button. Supply visible children or an accessible name; the trigger adds no fallback label. Pass render to the trigger to use another element. MenuContent defaults to the SDK placement behavior; side="bottom" and align="start" keep its start edge aligned with the reading direction in RTL.

Each MenuItem accepts a serializable value and reports it through Menu's onAction(value, details). UI SDK handles Enter, Space, ArrowDown, arrow navigation, typeahead, Escape, outside press, focus return, and disabled-item focus. It also supports groups, shortcuts, icons, async actions, and submenus through the exported SDK parts. A disabled item stays focusable but cannot run.

The OpenUI definition accepts a non-empty trigger label and an items array with one to six actions. Each action requires non-empty label and value strings. The optional danger and disabled flags default to false. At most one action can be destructive. The renderer validates these limits before rendering; invalid props produce a Menu render error through TensquadsRenderer's onError callback. OpenUI streams cannot serialize action functions. The OpenUI renderer dispatches a tensquads:menu-action CustomEvent on document with { value } in detail. A client can listen for that event and run the matching local action. Hand-built React menus use the UI SDK onAction(value, details) callback instead.

OpenUI places the destructive action last, after a separator. For hand-built React menus, place a MenuItem with destructive last and add the separator yourself. Menu styles use Agent-UI surface, border, shadow, radius, motion, and danger color tokens. Popup placement and collision handling come from UI SDK and follow page direction.

Import SegmentedControl, SegmentedControlItem and SegmentedControlIndicator from @tensquads/ui/react. They wrap UI SDK's public segmented-control parts from @ui-sdk/react/segmented-control and preserve their slots, render props, value callbacks and forwarded props.

Set a visible external label or aria-label. Put the indicator and two to four items inside the root. Each item needs a stable value. Use defaultValue or controlled value with onValueChange(value, details). Use this for exclusive modes, not actions.

UI SDK provides radio-group semantics, one tab stop, focus management, and arrow-key selection, skipping disabled items and wrapping by default. Left and right follow the page direction: in RTL, the physical arrow navigation reverses. Space selects the focused item; Enter submits its form.

The OpenUI definition accepts a label, two to four distinct text options and an optional initial value from those options. Its schema rejects duplicate options and values outside the option set. During streaming, each option keeps its identity as its text grows. Duplicate labels keep their item nodes. Only one copy is selectable: the focused copy, then the user-selected copy, then the first copy. Other copies are disabled until their text becomes distinct. An unmatched initial value is deferred, with the first available option selected until it matches. A user selection takes precedence over the initial value. Consumers can provide icon content through React children and must give icon-only items accessible names.

Import Squadmate and the SquadmateProps type from @tensquads/ui/squadmates or @tensquads/ui/react. The component renders an accessible agent image. It accepts an agent slug, an AgentState, a square pixel size (default 64), and a locale for the accessible name (default en). The image is not interactive and is not in the tab order.

The component takes a character slug such as petra. The roster and drawing APIs in @tensquads/ui/squadmates use role IDs such as master. Use AGENT_ROLE_TO_SLUG and AGENT_SLUG_TO_ROLE from @tensquads/ui/schemas to convert between them. That entry also exports AgentRoleSchema, AgentSlugSchema, and AgentStateSchema with their inferred types.

SQUADMATES contains the roster. AGENT_LOOP_STATES contains the loop states; SquadmateDrawState also includes idle. squadmateMarkup(imageId, state, size) returns SVG markup. It throws UnknownSquadmateError for an unknown role ID and UnknownSquadmateStateError for an unknown state. Sizes below 64 px show the upper body; sizes of 64 px or more show the whole mascot. SQUADMATE_CSS contains optional blink styles for inline markup and disables the animation for reduced motion. The React image does not include those styles.
The image name contains the localized character name and state. For example, English Petra, Planning and Arabic بترا، تخطيط.
Arabic names follow the website copy in tensquads-website/src/components/home/copy.ar.ts. English names follow its copy.en.ts entries and match the roster. Arabic state labels follow PLAN.md D18.

Mascot palettes and artwork colours are drawing source data in packages/ui/src/squadmates/mascots.ts. State badge colours are in packages/ui/src/squadmates/draw.ts. These colours are embedded in SVG markup. Roster colour fields remain source metadata in packages/ui/src/squadmates/roster.ts. They are not component CSS tokens.
OpenUI is useful when an agent needs to include an identified squadmate image in a generated response. The definition exposes the same props and validates them with shared schemas.

Import Switch and SwitchThumb from @tensquads/ui/react. They wrap the UI SDK switch parts from @ui-sdk/react/switch and preserve their slots, render props, checked state, callbacks and forwarded props.

Use defaultChecked or controlled checked with onCheckedChange(checked, details). Give the switch a visible external label or aria-label. disabled, readOnly, required, name and value follow the UI SDK API. Space toggles the switch; Enter does not.
The UI SDK implements switch semantics and keyboard handling. It does not use arrow navigation for a standalone switch. Track motion mirrors in RTL. Reduced-motion preferences disable the transition.

The OpenUI definition accepts a label, initial checked state and disabled state. During streaming, arriving initial values update the checked state until the user interacts. The user's choice takes precedence over later initial values.

Import Tooltip, its parts, and their prop types from @tensquads/ui/react. It wraps the UI SDK Tooltip from @ui-sdk/react/tooltip and keeps its root, trigger, content, arrow, and shortcut parts, data-slot values, render props, placement, open and delay options, and forwarded props.

Use Tooltip with TooltipTrigger and TooltipContent. TooltipArrow and TooltipShortcut are optional. UI SDK opens the hint on hover and keyboard focus and closes it on Escape. By default, it describes a named trigger with aria-describedby and names an unnamed trigger with the tooltip text. Set type="label" or type="description" to override this choice. Keep an icon-only button's own aria-label when the tooltip provides extra help. For touch-only help buttons, set toggleable.

TooltipContent accepts side and align values documented by UI SDK. start and end sides follow the reading direction, while data-side reports the physical side after placement and collision handling. The root accepts open, defaultOpen, delay, closeDelay, disabled, toggleable, closeOnPress, type, and shortcut props as documented by UI SDK.

The OpenUI definition accepts an accessible trigger label, short hint, and side. Fixtures render a named icon-only button with a tooltip because a tooltip has no meaningful standalone output without a trigger.
